# Using the Internet

The internet is one of the most important tools in modern life. People use it to communicate, learn, work, shop, watch videos, read news, and share information. Many everyday services now depend on the internet.

To use the internet effectively, it is helpful to understand how it works and how to find information online. People also need to understand how websites are organized and how to recognize reliable sources of information.

In this chapter, we will look at how the internet works, how web browsers and search engines help people explore the web, how to search for information more effectively, and how to understand website addresses and links.



## How the internet works

The internet is a global network of computers and devices connected to each other. These devices communicate using common technical rules called protocols. These rules allow information to travel from one device to another across many networks.

When a person connects to the internet, their device usually connects through an internet service provider. This provider may be a home broadband company, a mobile network, or a public network such as a university or library.

Information on the internet travels in small pieces called data packets. These packets move across many computers and network systems until they reach their destination.

For example, when you open a website, your device sends a request to a server. A server is a computer that stores websites and other online services. The server responds by sending the requested information back to your device. Your web browser then displays the webpage on your screen.

The internet includes many different services, such as websites, email systems, video streaming services, and online communication platforms. Even though these services look different to users, they all rely on the same underlying network connections.

Because the internet connects millions of computers around the world, it allows people to access information and communicate across long distances almost instantly.



## Web browsers and search engines

To access information on the internet, people usually use a program called a web browser.

A web browser is software that allows users to view and interact with websites. When a person enters a website address into the browser, the browser requests the webpage from the server and displays it on the screen.

Common web browsers include Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. Although they may look slightly different, they all perform the same basic functions. They allow users to visit websites, follow links, download files, and interact with online services.

Search engines are tools that help people find information on the web. Because there are billions of webpages online, it would be very difficult to find useful information without search tools.

A search engine works by indexing webpages across the internet. It collects information about many websites and stores this information in a large database.

When a user types a search query into a search engine, the system looks through its index and returns a list of results that are related to the search terms.

Popular search engines include Google, Bing, and DuckDuckGo. Each search engine uses its own methods to rank and display results.

Search engines make it possible to quickly find information, websites, images, videos, and many other types of content.



## How to search effectively

Searching the internet is easy, but finding the most useful information sometimes requires better search strategies.

One important step is choosing clear and specific keywords. Instead of typing a long question, it is often better to search using a few important words that describe the topic.

For example, instead of searching for a full sentence such as “How do I grow tomatoes in a small garden,” a user might search for “growing tomatoes small garden tips.”

Another useful method is refining the search if the first results are not helpful. Users can try different words, add more details, or remove words that may be confusing the search engine.

Search engines also allow users to place quotation marks around phrases to search for exact matches. This can help when looking for specific titles, quotes, or names.

Users should also look at several search results instead of only the first one. Sometimes useful information appears further down the list.

It is also important to think about the reliability of the source. Not every webpage contains accurate information. Good sources often include educational institutions, government organizations, established publications, or well-known experts.

Developing good search habits helps people find better information and avoid misleading content.



## Understanding websites and URLs

Every webpage on the internet has a unique address called a URL. URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. It tells the browser where to find a specific resource on the internet.

A typical URL has several parts.

The first part usually shows the protocol, such as http or https. The https version indicates that the connection between the browser and the website is encrypted, which provides better security.

The next part is the domain name. The domain name identifies the website. For example, in the address [https://example.com](https://example.com), the domain name is example.com.

Many websites also include additional paths after the domain name. These paths show the location of a specific page or file on the website.

For example, a URL might look like this:

[https://example.com/articles/digital-literacy](https://example.com/articles/digital-literacy)

In this case, the page is located inside a section called articles on the example.com website.

Understanding URLs can help users recognize where information is coming from. For example, a website ending in .gov often belongs to a government organization, while .edu usually belongs to an educational institution.

However, users should still evaluate websites carefully. A professional-looking webpage does not always guarantee accurate information.

Learning how websites and URLs work helps users navigate the internet more confidently and understand where online information comes from.

Using the internet effectively is an important part of digital literacy. By understanding how the internet works, how to search for information, and how to interpret website addresses, people can explore the online world more safely and efficiently.
